text:
alice: Quick heads-up — ran apples-vs-replay comparison for multi-tenant continuous-batching pool, found unexpected p95 skew for tenant T3. posting numbers + config.

ben: can you drop the harness config and the exact CLI you ran? :eyes:

alice: yes — used replay-harness v0.9.2 with sampled traces (prod-window=24h). cmd + config:
```bash
./replay_harness --pool=cont-batch-pool-7 --tenants-file=tenants.json \
  --replay=sampled_traces.tar --max-delay-ms=25 --batch-cap=1024 --cpu-threads=12
```
```json
{"prefix_cache":true,"kv_cache_hit_rate":0.86,"max_delay_ms":25,"batch_cap":1024}
```

carol: 0.86 kv hit rate looks fine. what was the p95 delta between synth and replay?

alice: synth p95 ~ 42ms, replay p95 ~ 98ms for T3 (other tenants ~45ms both). p50s aligned. So tail getting worse for that tenant only.

dinesh: interesting — single-tenant regressions usually kernel-selection related. multi-tenant skew smells like queueing + fairness. did you capture queuing traces?

alice: y, I collected runtime traces + per-request queue timestamps. attaching a short excerpt (converted):
```
[req 123] enqueued=1008 dequeue=1022 start_exec=1023 end_exec=1048
[req 456] enqueued=1010 dequeue=1030 start_exec=1031 end_exec=1045
[req 789 T3] enqueued=1005 dequeue=1055 start_exec=1056 end_exec=1085  <-- big wait
```

emily: that looks like head-of-line blocking where a long request holds the batch formation window open. what were the sequence lengths / KV cache miss patterns for T3?

alice: T3 has higher average seq len (1.9x) and slightly more KV misses (hit_rate ~0.72 vs pool 0.86). so slower decode + more compute per token and more cache fills.

ben: could be interplay: large seq + cache misses -> longer kernel exec -> continuous batching keeps pulling more small requests behind it -> they queue behind the long one until batch cap or max_delay triggers.

carol: do we have kernel latency distribution per model variant? maybe different kernel path chosen under those lengths.

alice: yes — profiler shows kernel selection flip from fast-f32-kernel to fp16-emulated fallback for sequences >1024 tokens (we tested an experimental quant path). The fallback adds ~18-25ms per token.

dinesh: so two axes: (1) kernel selection cliff at seq threshold, (2) KV-cache churn increasing per-request exec time. combined -> disproportionate tail for tenants with longer sequences.

emily: mitigation ideas:
- enforce per-tenant batch caps (e.g., tenant_batch_limit=64)
- shorter max_delay_ms for slices that hit heavy-cache churn
- size-aware kernel heuristic (prefer safer kernel if queue depth low)

ben: also consider prefilling KV cache for replay tests to normalize apples-to-apples — replay harness currently replays raw traces which may underrepresent warm-cache scenarios.

alice: good point — replay vs synth difference likely amplified by cache warmness. planning two followups:
1) run replay with kv-warmup pass (preload prefixes from traces) and compare p95
2) run microbench with per-tenant weighted queueing (simple round-robin across tenant buckets) and measure fairness metrics

perf-bot: perf-run scheduled: pr-4983-replay-fairness (job 3321). results expected in ~2h. :robot_face:

carol: also add a tiny experiment toggling batch-cap down to 256 — should reduce head-of-line wait by forcing earlier dispatch when big request present.

dinesh: can we add a metric to CI: tenant_p95_skew = max_tenant(p95)/median_tenant(p95) so changes that increase skew are flagged?

emily: yes, and add kv-cache-occupancy and kernel-switch-rate to the report. those two explain a lot of variance.

alice: I'll kick off the two runs (warmup + weighted-queue). posting links when jobs complete. TL;DR: root cause appears to be kernel selection cliff + KV cache churn causing long-exec requests to hold continuous-batching windows open; mitigations: tenant caps, lower max_delay, weighted-queue, warmup for apples-to-apples.

ben: awesome. if tests confirm, we should fast-track a guardrail: auto-detect tenant p95 skew >1.6 and apply tenant_batch_limit=64 as temporary mitigation.

alice: agreed. assigning follow-ups: @dinesh help design weighted-queue microbench, @carol add kernel-switch tracing to profiler, @emily add CI metrics. I'll own the replay warmup runs.

perf-bot: job 3321 finished — summary: replay-warmup improved T3 p95 from 98ms -> 56ms, weighted-queue reduced max tenant p95 skew from 2.3 -> 1.2. Full logs: https://perf.internal/reports/3321

ben: thats encouraging. let's reconvene after detailed logs. :thumbsup:

alice: thanks team — I'll open an RFC for guardrail + CI metrics later today.
